land.text: the Huainan command of Yang Xingmi, Prince of Wu from 902: central and southern Anhui, Jiangsu and much of Jiangxi

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Established: 902 (some historians), as a Tang-named princedom; independent from 907'.

land.text: the whole Wu realm: Xu Zhigao (Li Bian) overthrew Yang Pu in 937 and founded the Southern Tang on it

successors.note: Cliopatria draws this land under the label Southern Wu to 959 and starts its Southern Tang row only in 960.

capitals.name: Guangling (Yangzhou)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Guangling (present-day Yangzhou)'. The Five Dynasties page lists 'Guangling (Yangzhou), later Jinling (Nanjing)' for the Yang Wu; the move to Jinling belongs to the Southern Tang.

rulers.name: Yang Wo
rulers.note: The page lists 905-908 in the text and 907-908 in the infobox; his father Yang Xingmi (Prince of Wu 902, died 905) is the state's founder.

rulers.name: Yang Longyan
rulers.title: King of Wu from 919
rulers.note: The dated events say he died in 922.

rulers.name: Yang Pu
rulers.title: Emperor of Wu from 29 November 927
rulers.note: Xu Wen held real power under the Yang princes (regent to 927); Xu Zhigao after him.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 911 shape unchanged, valid from the Tang's fall in 907

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 907-910 (Cliopatria starts the state in 911): 'In 907 Zhu Wen forced the last Tang emperor to abdicate'; Yang Wo refused to recognize Later Liang and 'kept the last Tang era name', and Wu became sovereign from that point. The page says nothing about the extent in these years.

374,391 km2 against an infobox area given only as text, 'central and southern Anhui, central and southern Jiangsu, much of Jiangxi, and eastern Hubei': Anhui south of the Huai (about 100,000 km2), south and central Jiangsu (about 70,000), Jiangxi (about 167,000) and eastern Hubei (about 40,000) come to roughly 380,000 km2 (my own arithmetic from modern province areas, not from a page), so the shape and the infobox agree within a few percent; the bbox reaches 34.8 N and may overreach into northern Jiangsu. The shape is Southern Wu only to October 937: 'in October of the same year Yang Pu surrendered the state seal to him' (Southern Tang page), and the Southern Tang held the same land from then. Cliopatria runs the row to 946 here and to 959 below. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 911..937 from this entry's own 'valid 911-937 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

correction.text: not Southern Wu: this 495,453 km2 shape (bbox 23.49-34.81 N) is the Southern Tang realm of 947-959, which the southern-tang dossier should review under its own slug; the years 947-959 do not belong to southern-wu

keyframe_review.note: The state ended in 937, ten years before this shape begins ('The Southern Tang was founded by Li Bian in 937, when he overthrew emperor Yang Pu of Wu'). The extra 121,000 km2 over the 911 shape is the Southern Tang's conquests: Min's Jian and Ting prefectures (945) and Chu (951, 'territorial peak: 951' in the infobox); the Southern Tang then ceded Huainan to the Later Zhou in 958 ('Forced to cede Huainan'), so even as Southern Tang land the shape is too large for 958-959.

region.text: central and southern Anhui, central and southern Jiangsu, much of Jiangxi, and eastern Hubei: Yang Xingmi's Huainan command round Guangling (Yangzhou)

ledger.note: 907: with the Tang gone, Yang Wo holds Huainan without recognising the Later Liang. 'In 907 Zhu Wen forced the last Tang emperor to abdicate'; 'Yang Wo refused to acknowledge this change and continued the use of the last era name of Tang' and 'From this point Wu was an independent, sovereign entity'. The infobox gives 902 as the founding by some historians (Yang Xingmi, Prince of Wu from 902). The extent is the infobox's area text, not a dated boundary.

937: the Wu ends when Yang Pu hands the seal to Xu Zhigao. 'The Southern Tang was founded by Li Bian in 937, when he overthrew emperor Yang Pu of Wu'; 'In October of the same year Yang Pu surrendered the state seal to him, ending Yang rule of Wu'; 'On 11 November 937 Xu Gao formally ascended the throne.' The Yang Wu page: 'in 937 he formally seized power for himself by proclaiming himself King of Qi'; the Tang name came in 939.

wars.name: Wu-Wuyue border wars
wars.outcome: Intermittent fighting over border cities: Huainan forces attacked Hangzhou in 901-902 and withdrew; in 919 Qian Chuanguan won at Langshan but lost at Wuxi. No frontier change is recorded in 907-919.
wars.note: The Yang Wu page itself says only that there were undated clashes with Wuyue (Qian Liu) and with Later Liang (Zhu Wen).

certainty.note: The Wu realm is known by its circuits and prefectures; the Huai frontier with the Later Liang and the Yangtze-Min-Chu hill frontiers are approximate, and no treaty line is recorded.

notes: Cliopatria row Southern Wu 911-959 (2 shapes: 374,391 and 495,453 km2). Two problems: (1) the state ended in 937 (the Yang Wu page; the Southern Tang page dates the surrender of the seal to October 937 and the formal accession to 11 November), so the 947 shape (verdict wrong) and the 938-946 years of the 911 shape are Southern Tang land under a wrong label; Cliopatria's own Southern Tang row starts in 960, so the southern-tang dossier (another batch) must carry 937-959, taking the 911 shape from 938 and the 947 shape; it should list both Cliopatria Names or review these shapes as new keyframes. (2) Cliopatria's Wikipedia field 'Southern Wu' is a disambiguation page; the article is 'Yang Wu' (identity.wikipedia). The pages opened give no territorial gain or loss for the Wu (the Yang Wu page lists none; Jiangxi and Hubei appear only in the infobox area text), so the ledger holds only the founding and the end; the Jiangxi and Hubei parts of the shape rest on the infobox text, and the Huai frontier with the Later Liang is unverified (page budget). Not ledger events because they change no land: 919 Yang Longyan proclaims himself King of Wu; 29 November 927 Yang Pu becomes Emperor of Wu; 937 Xu Zhigao proclaims himself King of Qi. Date disagreements: the Yang Wu page puts Yang Wo's reign at 905-908 in the text and 907-908 in the infobox, and Yang Longyan's death in 922 against the list's 921; the Five Dynasties page puts the Wu at 902-937 in the text and 907-937 in the list. Counterpart Qi (Li Bian's own Qi, 937) is not a separate state here.
